主要内容: President Joe Biden has proposed increasing the top marginal income tax rate to 39.6% from 37% as part of his 2023 federal budget. This change would apply to married couples with taxable income over $450,000, heads of household with income above $425,000, and single filers earning more than $400,000. The proposal, which was previously floated by the administration, may face challenges in passing through Congress, especially with previous pushback from Senator Kyrsten Sinema and the upcoming midterm elections. Experts suggest that the tax hike may not be politically viable, as there were not enough lawmakers in favor of the change last year. The potential for the tax increase to take effect is after December 31, 2022, with income thresholds adjusting for inflation after 2023. President Joe Biden's 2023 federal budget proposal includes a tax hike on married filers with incomes exceeding $450,000. This proposal is part of his broader Build Back Better agenda. The budget also introduces a "billionaire minimum tax," which would impose a 20% income tax rate on the top 0.01% of earners and families with wealth exceeding $100 million. The 2017 tax overhaul, which temporarily reduced the top marginal rate to 37% through December 31, 2025, will automatically revert to 39.6% in January 2026 unless extended by Congress. These proposals are seen as potential challenges for policymakers due to their complexity and potential impact on high-income individuals and families.
